guide.note: The machined plate field: the top rail, the answer plate, the drag overlay. Inherited name; no longer any kind of guide-sign green. Theme-invariant.

signal.note: The one accent: the measured value on a plate, the live section in the rail, the primary action. Night value #ff7043.

ink.note: Body text on work surfaces. Night value #e9ebe8.

bg.note: The page ground. Steps up to panel (#ffffff) and raise (#f2f4f1). Night value #141615.

field-border.note: Interactive stroke; clears 3:1 on every surface in both themes. Night value #767d78.

work-zone.note: Status, fixed meaning: screening estimate, example values, sample file, draft method, review pending, validation level 0 or 1. Diamond glyph plus a word. Theme-invariant field with a black legend; work-zone-text is the text-safe variant.

warning.note: Status, fixed meaning: stale or needs re-checking. Diamond glyph plus a word, on the one pill in the system.

stop.note: Status, fixed meaning: refusal or error. Octagon glyph plus what is missing. Night value #ff8d80.

ok.note: Status, fixed meaning: checked. Check glyph plus the evidence line. Never the answer itself. Night value #5fd394.

service.note: Handoffs to other tools and sites, and the dashed comparison series. Arrow glyph plus destination. Night value #8fb6f2.

learn-text.note: Glossary terms and guides. Rectangle glyph. Night value #d8a87c.

heat-0.note: The one sequential ramp, six steps, light theme lightest-is-near-zero. Night inverts the order so the deep floor stays the low end.

plate-number.purpose: The measured value on a plate, in signal orange. Steps to plate-number-wide (4.25rem) at 768px and collapses to plate-number-inline (1.5rem) below 720px. The only type above 2rem.

plate-unit.purpose: The unit beside the number, baseline aligned, never inside it. Currency leads instead of trails.

tagline.purpose: The home page's one heading; 1rem below 720px.

title.purpose: Tool cell names and the rail wordmark.

subhead.purpose: h3 and a panel's inline summary heading.

body.purpose: Sentences. Prose 72ch, plate sentence 62ch, validation stamp 88ch.

body-small.purpose: Tool cell questions, field hints and errors, captions.

note.purpose: Validation stamp, screening strip, footer, rail navigation.

data.purpose: Roboto Mono for every number outside a plate, inputs, the command bar, receipts, citations. Always tabular-nums slashed-zero.

legend.purpose: The world's native label form: uppercase at wide tracking below body size, in muted (or legend-white at 0.72 on a plate). Only labels may use it.

band.purpose: The rating basis stamped along a plate's lower edge; 0.625rem on phones.

stamp.purpose: The PREVIEW mark on a tool cell.

shadows.name: plate
shadows.purpose: The answer plate, under its light top hairline and dark bottom hairline. The whole of content elevation.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Only the two layers that actually leave the page: the command-bar results list and the report dialog.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Every interactive element; switches to legend-white on the rail and on plates. Clears 7:1 against bg in both themes.

motion.name: component-state
motion.purpose: What the shipped component rules actually transition (background-color, border-color, color). Drift from the motion tokens, recorded as built. prefers-reduced-motion removes all of it.

narrative.overview:
Every number arrives the way an equipment rating does: engraved on a machined plate, with its rating basis stamped along the lower edge of that same plate, permanent and checkable. The plate is not a decoration applied to a result; it is the only form a measured number is allowed to take here.

The world is a machined dark shell carrying light work surfaces. The rail and the plates are cut from the same near-black field (guide); the page body and its panels are the pale metal the dense numbers actually live on. One orange (signal) owns the measured value, the live section in the rail, and the primary action, and owns nothing else: on a full home page it is three marks. Type is self-hosted: Archivo for display and UI, Roboto Mono for data and measurement, with tabular lining figures and a slashed zero wherever digits have to line up. Small labels are engraved legends, uppercase at wide tracking in sizes well under the body size.

Depth is machining, not lighting. A plate is a 1px light edge on top, a 1px dark edge underneath, and a 1px/2px shadow; nothing else is raised. There are no bevels, no gradients, no glass, no glow, and no tinted greys anywhere in the shipped CSS. Status has four reserved colours with fixed meanings, and each one is carried by a glyph and a word, never by hue alone.
keyCharacteristics: A measured number is always orange, always tabular, always on a dark plate, always above its basis band.
One signal orange; everything else is machined neutral.
Engraved legends: uppercase, 0.6875rem, 0.085em tracking, in muted.
Flat by construction: hairline edges, one 1px/2px plate shadow, one overlay shadow, nothing else.
Status reads without colour: glyph plus word, every time.
Both themes are first-class; night is the same machining in a dark room, never a glowing dashboard.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: signal paints the measured value, the live section in the rail, and the primary action. Nothing else. If a third orange mark appears in a viewport, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Full-Strength Rule
rules.body: A colour commits at full strength or not at all. The rail is a saturated field, never a tinted grey; data is never tinted for decoration; there are no alpha-blended brand washes. The only opacity in the system is the legible dimming of secondary legends on a plate (0.72-0.92).

rules.name: The Glyph-and-Word Rule
rules.body: Colour never carries meaning alone. Every status mark pairs a reserved colour with one of the five in-house glyphs and a word: diamond for estimate or stale, octagon for error, check for passed, arrow for handoff, rectangle for info.

rules.name: The Token-Only Rule
rules.body: No component rule contains a literal colour. verify/gates/style.mjs fails the build on any hex or colour function in a hand-written stylesheet, and recomputes every contrast pairing in both themes.

rules.name: The Engraved Legend Rule
rules.body: Small labels are uppercase at wide tracking in a size below the body size, in muted (or white at 0.72 on a plate). This is the world's native label form, and it is the only thing that may be set in it: a sentence, a value, or a navigation item never takes legend styling.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any digit that might line up with another digit is set with tabular-nums slashed-zero - plate numbers, table cells, receipts, inputs, axes. A number that shifts when it updates is a bug.

rules.name: The Unit-Beside Rule
rules.body: The unit sits beside the number at plate-unit or label size, baseline aligned, never inside the number and never the same size as it. Currency is the one inversion: $ leads at unit size.

rules.name: The Basis Band Rule
rules.body: A plate never ships without the band stamped along its lower edge: source, interval count, date range, as-of, validation. At every width, in every rendition, including the one-line phone plate. A measured number without its basis is the one thing this world refuses.

rules.name: The Ruled Index Rule
rules.body: Repeating navigational rows are ruled, not boxed. A card border around every item in a list is wrong here; one hairline between items is right.

rules.name: The Two-Hairline Rule
rules.body: A raised surface is a light 1px top edge and a dark 1px bottom edge in its own colour family, and at most a 1px/2px shadow. If a surface needs more than that to read as raised, it is not raised; it is a different surface.

rules.name: The Detached-Only Rule
rules.body: The 0 8px 24px shadow is reserved for layers that actually leave the page - the command results and the dialog. Nothing anchored in the document flow gets it.

dos: Do put every measured number on a plate, in signal, with its unit beside it and its basis band stamped along the lower edge - at every width.
Do keep orange to three marks: the measured value, the live section, the primary action.
Do pair every status colour with its glyph and its word, using the five in-house glyph shapes.
Do set small labels as engraved legends (uppercase, 0.6875rem, 0.085em, muted) and nothing else in that style.
Do take every colour, space, and radius from site/styles/tokens.mjs; the style gate fails on a literal colour.
Do build raised surfaces from a light top hairline, a dark bottom hairline, and at most a 1px/2px shadow.
Do rule repeating rows instead of boxing them.
Do check both themes, 320px, keyboard-only, and forced-colors before shipping a surface.
donts: Don't use a bevel, gradient, glass, backdrop blur, glow, or a second content elevation. The 0 8px 24px shadow belongs to detached overlays only.
Don't tint a grey to suggest a brand, or tint data for decoration. Colour commits at full strength or not at all.
Don't spend signal on a heading, a border, an icon, or a chart series that is measured truth; measured series are graphite.
Don't use work-zone for errors or warning for estimates; the four status meanings are fixed.
Don't ship a plate, a rendition of a plate, or a copied result without its basis and its validation level.
Don't introduce a type size outside the ramp, a radius between 6px and 10px, or a spacing value off the s1-s8 scale.
Don't request a font weight outside Archivo's 400-700 or Roboto Mono's 400-500; font-synthesis-weight: none means it will silently render at the nearest shipped weight.
Don't load a font, icon set, or stylesheet from a CDN. Everything is self-hosted.
Don't reintroduce the retired highway-sign world: green fields, Overpass, federal sign colours, shields, or reflective-gradient effects.
Don't put more than one answer plate in a viewport.
